Tasks and labels

tasks.Rmd

This chapter builds a TaskCpt, lists the labels it accepts and sets out the coordinates of a labelled region. A task holds the sequences and their labels, and learners, measures and plots all read from it.

library(mlr3)
library(mlr3changepoint)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

Building a task

A task has one row per sequence. The data needs two list columns: one holds the signal as a numeric vector, the other a data.table(start, end, label) of labelled regions. Sequences can differ in length and in their number of labels.

set.seed(36)
cpt_data = data.table(
  signal = list(c(rnorm(100, 18), rnorm(100, 36), rnorm(100, 9)), rnorm(100, 0)),
  label = list(
    data.table(start = c(90, 190), end = c(110, 210), label = "1change"),
    data.table(start = 1, end = 100, label = "0changes")
  )
)

TaskCpt$new() takes the name of the label column as target and the name of the signal column as sequence. label_type sets the label vocabulary.

task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy", backend = cpt_data,
  target = "label", sequence = "signal", label_type = "changepoint"
)
task
#> 
#> ── <TaskCpt> (2x1) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Target: label
#> • Properties: -
task$label_type
#> [1] "changepoint"

$truth() returns the labelled regions, one table per sequence.

task$truth()
#> [[1]]
#>    start   end   label
#>    <num> <num>  <char>
#> 1:    90   110 1change
#> 2:   190   210 1change
#> 
#> [[2]]
#>    start   end    label
#>    <num> <num>   <char>
#> 1:     1   100 0changes

The signal column has the role sequence, so it is not a feature. Learners compute their own features from it.

task$col_roles$sequence
#> [1] "signal"

Changepoint labels

With label_type = "changepoint", a label gives the number of changes a region may contain. The names come from penaltyLearning::change.labels, which also accepts synonyms.

Label Synonyms Changes in the region
0changes normal, 0breakpoints none
1change 1breakpoint exactly one
>0changes breakpoint, >0breakpoints at least one

A segmentation with more changes in a region than its label allows has a false positive there. One with fewer changes than the label needs has a false negative.

Peak labels

With label_type = "peak", the signal is a sequence of non-negative integer counts, and the labels come from the PeakError package.

Label Meaning
noPeaks no peak overlaps the region
peaks at least one peak overlaps the region
peakStart exactly one peak starts in the region
peakEnd exactly one peak ends in the region

The first sequence below has a burst of counts at positions 61 to 100, inside a peaks region.

set.seed(36)
peak_data = data.table(
  counts = list(c(rpois(60, 2), rpois(40, 25), rpois(100, 2)), rpois(200, 2)),
  label = list(
    data.table(start = c(1, 55), end = c(50, 105), label = c("noPeaks", "peaks")),
    data.table(start = 10, end = 190, label = "noPeaks")
  )
)
peak_task = TaskCpt$new(
  id = "toy_peak", backend = peak_data,
  target = "label", sequence = "counts", label_type = "peak"
)
peak_task
#> 
#> ── <TaskCpt> (2x1) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Target: label
#> • Properties: -

Coordinates

Positions are 1-based indices into the signal. The two label types read start and end differently, because a change sits between two points and a peak covers points.

A change at X lies between positions X and X + 1. A changepoint region is open on the left and closed on the right, (start, end], so it holds the changes with start < X <= end. The region from 90 to 110 holds the changes at 91 to 110. A region from start = 0 to end = n covers every change a sequence of n points can have. A region that starts at 1, as in the toy above, leaves out a change between the first two points.

A peak region covers positions start to end, both included. A predicted peak counts for noPeaks and peaks when it overlaps those positions, and for peakStart and peakEnd when its first or last position falls inside them.

autoplot() shades each region so that a predicted mark lies inside the shading exactly when the measures count it inside the region. Changes are drawn halfway between two positions.

autoplot(task)

The peak task uses the colours of the PeakError labels.

autoplot(peak_task)

Each sequence gets its own panel. To plot part of a large task, filter a copy first, for example task$clone()$filter(1:4).
